About us

Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform, on a mission to help more people invest, and invest well.

We’re building the infrastructure behind the next generation of investing. Our technology already powers some of the UK’s most ambitious fintechs, banks, financial advisers and wealth firms, with close to a million investors relying on Seccl-powered platforms. And we’re now expanding into Europe.

We’ve got a proven product, strong momentum and big ambitions for what comes next: helping more household-name brands launch and scale investment propositions, entering new markets and replacing outdated investment infrastructure with technology that’s faster, simpler and built for scale.

We’re proud to be part of Octopus, one of the UK’s most successful privately held investment and technology groups. That gives us the backing and long-term perspective to build something substantial, while keeping the pace and energy of a high-growth business. Seccl and Octopus are both B Corp certified and share a belief that profit and purpose should go hand in hand.

If you want to help shape the future of investing in the UK and across Europe, you’ll be in good company.

Check out the Seccl website to see what we’re building and read more about our mission to shape the future of investments.

The role

We’re looking for an engineering manager to lead one of our product engineering squads, reporting to an engineering director. As Seccl grows and our platform supports more customer firms and investors, you’ll help your squad deliver the scalable platform capability we need for what comes next.

You’ll build a strong, psychologically safe engineering team where people feel trusted, supported and able to do their best work. You’ll coach and develop engineers, create clarity and help the team maintain high standards while delivering valuable outcomes.

Working closely with your product manager, engineering leaders and teams across Seccl, you’ll help define priorities and keep the squad focused on the right outcomes. You’ll balance delivery pace with engineering quality, security, operational resilience and long-term maintainability.

This role brings together people leadership, delivery and engineering accountability. You’ll stay close enough to the technology to guide and challenge decisions, while giving engineers the ownership and support they need to develop effective solutions.

What you’ll own

  • Building, leading and developing an inclusive, high-performing engineering squad

  • Creating an environment of trust, psychological safety, continual learning and constructive challenge

  • Owning the delivery health of your squad, from priorities and planning through to production readiness, reliability and ongoing maintainability

  • Partnering with product managers to align the squad’s work with customer, commercial, regulatory and platform priorities

  • Guiding technical decisions and helping the team build solutions that are scalable, secure, resilient and well integrated with the wider platform

  • Using metrics, feedback and team insight to improve delivery predictability, system reliability and team effectiveness

  • Recruiting and onboarding engineers while contributing to shared engineering practices and collaboration across Seccl

This role’s for you if...

  • You’re an experienced engineering manager who has led teams working within complex product or technology domains

  • You have a strong track record of hiring, onboarding, coaching and developing engineers

  • You can balance people leadership with delivery accountability and remain close enough to the technology to offer meaningful guidance

  • You have experience with a modern JavaScript and cloud-based technology stack. Our stack includes Node.js, JavaScript and TypeScript, MongoDB, AWS, Lambda and Serverless Framework

  • You communicate clearly and can work effectively with product managers, engineering leaders and senior stakeholders

  • You have recent, practical experience with AI-assisted engineering tools and can help teams use them responsibly to improve delivery, quality and developer effectiveness

  • You care about building secure, scalable and resilient systems. Experience in financial services, fintech, investment platforms or another regulated environment would be valuable

This role isn’t for you if...

  • You’re looking for a purely people-management role. You’ll need enough technical credibility to guide decisions and challenge constructively

  • You want to be the primary technical decision-maker. You’ll create the environment for engineers to own solutions and grow their capability

  • You need priorities to remain fixed. You’ll be leading delivery in a fast-moving environment where plans and business needs can change

  • You prioritise speed at the expense of quality. Delivery pace matters, alongside security, resilience and long-term maintainability

What’s in it for you

We offer a generous mix of benefits designed around the things that matter to our people:

  • 💰 £95,000 to £110,000 depending on experience, reviewed annually, plus a 6% employer pension contribution and life assurance

  • 🌴 27 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, your birthday off and paid dependant leave

  • 💙 Two volunteering days each year

  • 🌎 The option to work abroad for up to six weeks a year

  • 🌟 Secclbrate, our recognition programme offering flexible rewards including extra pay, additional holiday and increased learning budget

  • 🏅 One-month paid sabbatical after eight years

  • 🏥 Private medical insurance with AXA Health

  • 👪 Enhanced parental leave

  • 💻 MacBook and up to £500 towards your home office set-up

  • 📖 £750 annual learning budget

  • 🌻 Health and wellbeing support, including free therapy through Wellness Cloud and mental health support through Headspace

  • 🌱 Financial wellbeing benefits, including Octopus Money, the Octopus Share Incentive Plan and will writing through Octopus Legacy

  • 🎁 Perkbox, with flexible points and a range of discounts and perks

  • 🚲 Access to Cycle to Work and Octopus Electric Vehicle Leasing

Our culture

We put people first and try hard to create an environment where people feel trusted, heard and able to do their best work.

We value openness, curiosity and different perspectives. You’ll have the freedom to challenge how things are done, experiment with better ways of working and take real ownership of your impact.

Check out our Glassdoor page for the latest reviews or our LinkedIn for company updates and insights from the team.

Interview process

Interviewing is a two-way process. Our interviews are conversational, with plenty of time for you to get to know us and ask questions too.

  • Initial conversation: a chat with someone from our Talent team about your experience, what you’re looking for and the role

  • System design interview: a 60-minute technical conversation exploring how you approach architecture, trade-offs and complex engineering decisions

  • Leadership interview: a 45-minute conversation focused on people leadership, delivery and cross-functional collaboration

  • Bar raiser: a 45-minute conversation with colleagues from outside the immediate team, focused on our operating principles and how you approach your work

We review applications as they come in and may close the role once we have enough candidates to move forward. We’ll keep you updated throughout.

Everyone’s welcome

We want to build a diverse and inclusive company full of brilliant people with different skills, experiences and perspectives. All applicants will be considered without regard to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran status, neurodiversity or disability.

If this sounds like your kind of thing, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to hear from you.

Der ultimative TYPO3-Check

Du bist bei uns richtig, wenn du…

  • … bei „Wir brauchen nur ein kleines Feld mehr im Backend“ im Kopf schon TCA, Datenbank-Migration und die drei Fluid-Templates aufklappst, die es wirklich braucht.

  • … für dein wichtigstes Werkzeug hältst. Direkt nach dem Cache-Leeren.

  • … beim Satz „Das ging in TYPO3 v7 aber noch“ freundlich lächelst und den Extension Scanner startest.

  • … und dein Gewissen dir verbietet, freitags um 16 Uhr ein Major-Update auf Production zu schieben. Auch nicht „nur schnell“.

… dann gilt für uns nur noch eins: composer require netfed/du

Worum geht es?

Du verantwortest die TYPO3-Technik großer Corporate-Websites. Von der Aufwandsschätzung über Konzeption und Neuaufbau bis zu Weiterentwicklung, Support und Updates. Du berätst Kolleg:innen und Kunden und sorgst dafür, dass unsere Projekte auf einem sauberen technischen Fundament stehen.

Warum diese Rolle bei uns anders ist?

Wir arbeiten für namhafte Konzerne und große Mittelständler, bei denen die Website ein strategisches Aushängeschild ist. Du baust hier nicht Website Nummer 47 nach Schema F. Du triffst die technischen Entscheidungen und verantwortest die Architektur. Dabei vertrauen wir voll auf deine Erfahrung. Dazu kommen eine eigene, von uns betriebene Cloud-Hosting-Umgebung und eine gelebte DevOps-Kultur, die sich am Stand der Technik orientiert.

Und was ist mit KI?

Gehört bei uns zum Alltag. Nicht als Pilotprojekt, sondern als Werkzeug. Du arbeitest mit KI als Sparringspartner: beim Refactoring, beim Testen, beim Dokumentieren, beim schnellen Zweitblick auf eine Migration. Die KI schlägt vor, du entscheidest. Genau deshalb suchen wir jemanden mit echter TYPO3-Erfahrung, der erkennt, wann ein Vorschlag gut ist und wann er Unsinn ist.

  • Du erstellst die technische Konzeption neu aufzubauender TYPO3-Websites.

  • Du verantwortest die TYPO3-Aspekte großer Kundenprojekte: Aufwandsschätzung, Neuaufbau, Weiterentwicklung, Support und Updates.

The role

ClickUp's Cloud Platform team builds scalable, secure, and cost-efficient AWS infrastructure, with a heavy focus on Amazon EKS, that stays ahead of product and enterprise growth.   • Identify improvement opportunities and emerging risks, and propose novel solutions that improve reliability, scalability, and cost efficiency before constraints become blockers.

  • Automate shard buildouts and implement Terraform guardrails and hardened ingress that reduce incidents.

  • Scale systems for multi-shard, multi-region growth while meeting compliance attestations (SOC 2, ISO 27001, etc), disaster recovery, and enterprise security requirements.

  • Partner with SRE, Security, product, AI, and enterprise teams to bridge infrastructure and product engineering.

  • Own the reliability of Cloud Platform itself: on-call, incident response, postmortems, runbooks, and prevention.

  • Use AI tooling daily to accelerate development, testing, IaC, operations, and investigations, and help the team raise its AI leverage.

What we're looking for

  • 6+ years building and operating large-scale distributed systems with a focus on infrastructure and cloud, especially compute foundations.

  • Deep, hands-on experience operating and troubleshooting Kubernetes in production, including control-plane, node, and networking issues, ideally Amazon EKS at fleet scale.

  • Strong AWS experience: EKS, EC2, Lambda, API Gateway, VPC networking, IAM, S3, KMS. Bedrock is a plus.

  • Multi-account AWS (20+ accounts) experience, including Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, VPC routing, DNS, and load balancing.

About the role

We are hiring an Accounting Automation Engineer to replace manual accounting work across a multi-entity, multi-country enterprise, using Claude Code and agentic AI.

You will use Claude Code and agentic AI, plus Python or JavaScript/TypeScript, to automate accounts payable, accounts receivable, reconciliations, month-end close and the wider day-to-day accounting operation. You need strong IFRS or US GAAP knowledge to get the numbers right, because an automation that posts wrong entries is worse than no automation.

We build agentic AI systems and AI agents, not fixed step-by-step workflows. Experience with rule-based workflow builders such as n8n or Zapier is not relevant to this role.

Titles we will consider: Accounting Automation Engineer, Finance Engineer, Financial Systems Engineer, Technical Accountant (with engineering background), Accounting Systems Manager (with engineering background).

Key Responsibilities

The goal is to automate the repeatable core of enterprise accounting, with human review kept only where judgment is needed.

Accounts payable

  • Invoice capture and data extraction from PDFs and email, using AI where useful

  • Vendor matching, coding suggestions, and 2-way/3-way PO matching

  • Duplicate invoice detection and approval routing

  • Payment run preparation and vendor statement reconciliation

Accounts receivable

  • Invoice generation and delivery

  • Cash application and bank receipt matching

  • Aging reports, dunning and collections reminders

  • Credit note handling and bad debt/ECL provision support

Reconciliations

  • Bank and card reconciliations across all accounts and currencies

  • Balance sheet account reconciliations (prepayments, accruals, deferred revenue, fixed assets)

  • Intercompany and subledger-to-GL reconciliations

  • Exception reports that flag only the items a human needs to review

Month-end close

  • Close checklist tracking and scheduled reminders

  • Recurring, accrual, prepayment and amortization journals

  • Depreciation runs and FX revaluation

  • Trial balance checks, flux/variance analysis, and draft commentary

  • Management reporting packs

General accounting operations

  • Expense report and employee reimbursement checks

  • Chart of accounts and master data hygiene

  • Audit support: evidence collection, PBC lists, sample extraction

  • Data pipelines between ERP, banks, payment platforms and spreadsheets

Qualifications

  • Experience reconciling payment processor statements across multiple jurisdictions and currencies

  • Experience with shared cost services that invoice group companies, including complex expense splits and automated invoice generation

  • Experience with an ERP and its API (which ERP does not matter)

  • Knowledge of VAT/GST and e-invoicing rules in several jurisdictions

  • Additional languages, where our entities operate in non-English markets

Exa is building a search engine for the AI era. Our Search API currently powers Agents, Fortune 500s, and AI labs as we transform an industry that hasn't been disrupted since the 90s. We're high agency, low-ego, and united by the feeling that this is one of the last problems worth getting right.

 

About the role

Forward Deployed Engineers are the technical tip of the spear at Exa. Partnered with an Account Executive, you own the technical win: you run discovery with customer engineering teams, design solutions on Exa's API, build and deliver demos and POCs that prove value, and turn technical evaluations into closed deals. You'll be one of the first GTM engineers in your region — you'll help define how Exa sells there, not just execute a playbook.

In this role, you will:

  • Own the technical side of the sales cycle: discovery, solution design, demos, POCs/POVs, and technical objection handling, in partnership with your AE

  • Run the technical side of expansion: spot new use cases in existing accounts and turn them into evaluations, with your AE

  • Build working demos and prototypes on Exa's API tailored to each customer's use case — agents, research, search, enrichment

  • Tell the story: translate Exa's capabilities into use-case narratives that land with CTOs, engineers, and PMs alike

  • Be the trusted technical advisor: know Exa inside out — the product, the API, the problems it solves — answer hard questions honestly, run evaluations rigorously, and know when to pull in engineering

  • Feed the field back into product: identify patterns across customer evaluations and channel them to product and engineering

  • Scale yourself and the region: build reusable demos, integration patterns, and playbooks, and represent Exa at technical workshops, meetups, and conferences

  • As a founding regional hire, support early customers through onboarding and initial implementation while we build out dedicated post-sales

Requirements

  • 5+ years in a customer-facing technical role (flexible for exceptional candidates) — solutions/sales engineering, solutions architecture, or an engineering role with heavy customer exposure (e.g., engineering lead, developer relations, technical consulting)

  • Technical depth with APIs and modern development (e.g. Python or TypeScript): you can design an integration, build a working demo, and debug it live — using AI-assisted tooling is expected, hand-crafted code is not the bar

  • Strong communication and presentation skills: you can command a room, adapt to your audience, and say "I don't know — I'll find out" when you don't

  • Comfort with ambiguity and early-stage intensity: you can run several evaluations in parallel, prioritize what moves deals, and your job description will change as the region grows

  • Familiarity with the modern AI stack — LLMs, RAG, agents — and how customers evaluate it; you can scope a POC with clear success criteria

  • Based in region with willingness to travel for customer engagements

You might excel if you…

🏨 The Company

Resilience Care is a leading medical remote monitoring player and a clinical research partner. Founded in France in 2021, our mission is simple: improve patient care.

We build remote monitoring solutions in oncology, gastroenterology and psychiatry, powered by ePRO collection and AI techniques. Our platform helps care teams detect side effects early for continuous and proactive care, while our patient app helps people track and manage symptoms with tailored resources.

Our solutions optimize care pathways, enrich continuous patient understanding, and accelerate clinical research through the collection, structuring and detailed analysis of real-world data. Today, our solutions are deployed in routine care for 35,000 patients across 200+ healthcare institutions, and also support around twenty academic and industry clinical studies.

We put data at the service of care and therapeutic innovation, with the ambition to enable every patient to benefit from personalized medicine.

📝 Your role

In a nutshell: You join the Data Reliability Engineering (DRE) team to build, operate and secure the data platform that carries healthcare data from our production services to the people who use it — internal operational teams, clinical research users, and external partners receiving contractual data exports.

Your impact: Data arrives on time, complete, traceable and secure — and when it doesn't, we know before the users do. You turn one-off data requests and manual export procedures into automated, monitored, reproducible pipelines.

Your day-to-day:

  • Build and operate data pipelines : ingestion from application events & databases, transformation, export.
  • Build the tooling that handles those pipelines, hand in hand with SRE: infrastructure as code (Terraform, Helm on Kubernetes), deployment, CI/CD, secrets management, database operations and incident response.
  • Watch over data quality and pipeline health: Grafana dashboards, alerting, and metric- and log-based observability, so failures are detected and diagnosed fast.
  • Own data contracts and data quality: agree with the emitting squads on schemas, semantics and breaking-change rules, and enforce them with automated tests (freshness, completeness, referential integrity) that fail loudly before the data reaches its users.
  • Deliver secure data exports to external partners and institutions.
  • Provision and maintain dedicated PostgreSQL Research Spaces for clinical study teams, including access control and data scoping per study.
  • Help the modelers scale their work: industrialize the dbt project so a single modelisation written by a Data Analyst is centralized, parallelized and applied across several targets.
  • Work directly with the requesters: scope the need, challenge it, agree on what is feasible, deliver, and document.
  • Work with the product squads on the data they emit: challenge their design upstream, and take part in the implementation on their side (TypeScript) when needed — you contribute to their code, they keep their roadmap.
  • Participate in code reviews, technical design and continuous improvement of engineering standards.

✨ Your team

  • Your future teammates: Mélody Ballouard and Alric Gaurier — Data Reliability Engineers.

The team owns the data pipeline end to end: ingestion, transformation, exports, and the infrastructure underneath. You'll be exposed to all of it from day one.

  • Your manager: Alric Gaurier
  • Team's extra: A small team with direct exposure to clinical research, medical and operational stakeholders. What you build is used by named people you talk to every week — not by an anonymous backlog.

👤 What we are looking for

  • ⚙️ You are the right person if you can:
    • Ship production-grade Python (tests, typing, code quality, reviews, CI), and use AI tools as a multiplier without letting go of engineering ownership.
    • Build and operate data pipelines and orchestration (Prefect, Airflow, Dagster or equivalent), including event streams (Kafka) and object/file transports (S3, SFTP).
    • Write and optimize advanced SQL on PostgreSQL (indexing, query plans, incremental loads).
    • Push dbt well beyond basic usage: macros and Jinja, multi-target projects, incremental strategies, tests, packages and CI integration.
    • Deploy and operate what you build (Terraform, Helm/Kubernetes, containers, CI/CD), with meaningful monitoring and alerting (Grafana or equivalent) — and lead the diagnosis when something breaks.
    • Read and contribute to TypeScript codebases when the pipeline meets the application side, with a solid grasp of back-end API architecture (REST design, versioning, authentication, pagination, contracts).
  • 🙂 You are the right person if you have:
    • Strong communication skills — this is not a nice-to-have in this role. You will spend real time with non-technical requesters.
    • The ability to translate an operational or scientific need into a technical specification, and to say no (and explain why) when a request is not feasible or not compliant — with the support of the Legal/Compliance department.
    • Comfort collaborating with SRE on shared infrastructure, and with scientific profiles on clinical trial data.
    • Rigor with sensitive data: you treat patient data with the caution it deserves, by reflex.
    • Ownership, autonomy and accountability, including on-call-style responsibility for what you ship — with a structured, detail-oriented approach, a bias for automation, and a focus on impact and maintainability.
    • Curiosity and a continuous-learning mindset — the reflex to go beyond your own stack: reading a product squad's code, digging into an API or an infrastructure layer you don't own, and learning what you need to unblock yourself instead of waiting for someone else.
  • 📃 You are the right person if you have already:
    • ~4–6 years in data engineering, platform engineering, or backend with a strong infrastructure component.
    • Operated production pipelines you were accountable for (not just built them).
    • Written and reviewed infrastructure as code in a team setting.
    • Delivered data to stakeholders outside your own team, and handled the conversation that goes with it.
    • Worked in a maintained codebase (Git workflow, PRs, CI).
    • Operated in a context with high standards (security, compliance, sensitive data).
  • It's a plus if you:
    • Have exposure to healthcare data, GDPR-heavy or HDS-hosted environments.
    • Have supported scientific or clinical research users (study datasets, cohort extraction, data requests from investigators).
    • Have handled contractual data exchanges with external partners (data transfer agreements, delivery SLAs, encryption requirements).
💛 Why join us?

  • A mission that holds up: improving patient care with data.
  • Real ownership over a full platform — pipelines and the infrastructure they run on — not a narrow slice.
  • Direct contact with the people your work serves, including clinical research teams running active studies.
  • A culture focused on automation, observability and continuous improvement, with practical AI usage.
  • Remote-friendly setup and an environment that values quality, standards and ownership.

Hiring process

  • Screening - Elena (15 min): validate motivation and role prerequisites
  • Manager Fit - Alric (30 min): position fit, and an honest conversation about the ops-and-build nature of the role
  • Technical Case Study - live session (1h30), no preparation: you work through a small realistic case with us — pipeline design, infrastructure and data export constraints. We look at how you reason and what you ask, not at a polished deliverable.
  • Team fit : Fit interview Mellody, Anna, Guillaume (30 min): collaboration fit with Research/Clinical and operational requesters
  • Culture fit - Elena (40 min): assess alignment with our culture and remote ways of working
  • Strategic Fit Jullian (30 min): collaboration fit, engineering standards

Diplômé en informatique, vous affichez une solide expérience en développement back-end et full-stack .NET Core, dans des environnements distribués et orientés micro-services.

Deine Rolle

Wir bauen Renewa One – das zentrale System, mit dem wir die Sanierung von Gebäuden managen. Wir entwickeln radikal anders als die meisten: KI-first mit Claude Code. Der Code entsteht schnell und in großer Menge – die eigentliche Kunst liegt nicht mehr im Tippen, sondern im Beurteilen, Zusammenführen und Verantworten.


Deine Mission

  • Du entwickelst neue Features unseres Sanierungs-Management-Systems – KI-assistiert und auf Basis unserer bestehenden Architektur.
  • Du bringst Pull Requests verlässlich zum Release: reviewen, testen, Konflikte lösen und dafür geradestehen, dass nur sauberer, korrekter Code live geht.
  • Du bist die entscheidende Qualitätsinstanz für KI-generierten Code – du erkennst die subtilen Fehler, die eine grüne Pipeline nicht sichtbar macht.
  • Du hältst die Codebase konsistent und wartbar: gemeinsame Muster und ein sauberes Datenmodell statt Wildwuchs.
  • Du verantwortest den Weg von der Idee bis zum Release mit – damit Features schnell und in guter Qualität bei den Nutzern ankommen.


Dein Profil

  • Erfahrung mit Claude Code: Du entwickelst KI-first mit Claude Code (oder vergleichbaren KI-Coding-Agents) und prüfst generierten Code kritisch, statt ihn blind zu übernehmen. Bei uns ist das die Grundlage der Arbeit, kein Bonus.
  • Full-Stack-TypeScript mit echter Tiefe: Du bist im Frontend (React) sattelfest und kannst Backend-Code – APIs, Datenbank-Queries, Services – selbst schreiben und korrigieren. Nur so kannst du ihn wirklich beurteilen statt nur durchwinken. 
  • Urteilsvermögen fürs Merge-Gate: Du liest Pull Requests kritisch, gibst klares, konstruktives Feedback und übernimmst Verantwortung dafür, was released wird. 
  • PostgreSQL & Datenmodellierung: Du verstehst Transaktionen, Indizes, Fremdschlüssel und Migrationen – und behandelst das Schema als langlebigen Contract, nicht als Wegwerfartikel.
  • Sauberes Git-Handwerk: Rebase, Merge-Konflikte, CI-Pipelines und ein Branch-basierter Workflow sind für dich Alltag.
  • Disziplin statt Ego: Du arbeitest mit den bestehenden Mustern des Teams, statt bei jedem PR deine eigene Meinung durchzudrücken.
  • Du wohnst bereits in Hamburg: Diese Stelle ist nicht remote zu besetzen. Du solltest bereits in Hamburg oder im Umland wohnen und bereit sein, mehrmals in der Woche aus unserem Büro in Winterhude zu arbeiten.
  • Deutschkenntnisse auf C-Level: Um intern gut mit unseren Mitarbeitenden zu kommunizieren und ein Verständnis für ihre Wünsche und die fachlichen Ansprüche zu entwickeln, sind sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse notwendig. 
Schöne Extras:
  • Erfahrung mit Fly.io / Docker und der Anbindung externer APIs (z. B. CRM- oder Buchhaltungssysteme)
  • Blick für UI-Konsistenz und Design-Systeme
  • Interesse an der Bau- / Sanierungs-Domäne
